To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CAPM is not relevant for tests of the semi strong form efficiency for the Nigerian Stock Market because it understates portfolio risk, and that the market skewness and co skewness factors can be a risk reducing strategy for investors in response to anticipated adverse changes in the riskiness of the market portfolio.

the asset pricing model consisting of the market portfolio plus the skewness or co-skillness factor and the portfolio idiosyncra tic volatility factor best explains the risk return trade offs of portfolios on the NSE and that an asset pricing specification that includes the market portfolio alone underestimates portfolio risk.
the CAPM is not an adequate asset pricing model for tests of market efficiency on the NSE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how relevant the CAPM is for studies of market efficiency on the Nigerian Stock Market, and how non synchronous trading of stock affects portfolio risk return trade off.
the relevance of the CAPM for tests of the efficient market hypothesis on the NSE.
the effects of non-synchronous trading on the pricing of risk on the Nigerian Stock Market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our findings are in line with the view that the Nigerian Stock Market is not semi-strong form efficient.
the market skewness and co skewness factors are relevant for the Nigerian Stock Market.
the CAPM is not relevant for tests of the semi strong form efficiency hypothesis of the Nigerian Stock Exchange.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

while non synchronous trading of shares on the Nigerian Stock Market is not a significant impediment for the achievement of portfolio diversification, it is a factor that induces greater risk aversion and hence a higher price for risk.
the CAPM is not a relevant asset pricing model for testing semi strong form efficiency on the Nigerian Stock Market.

while the CAPM remains a relevant asset pricing model for tests of market efficiency on the NSE, its one factor specification is inappropriate for this purpose and a multi factor specification which consists of the portfolio market portfolio, market skewness or market co skewness, and portfolio idio syncratic volatility factors is a more appropriate specification for this purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAPM is not a useful model of asset pricing for tests of market efficiency on the Nigerian Stock Market.
the CAPM is not an appropriate asset pricing model for studies of the efficiency of stock markets.

the conventional one factor specification is not an appropriate representation of portfolio risk return tradeoffs in the Nigerian Stock Market, and that the effects of non-synchronous trading of stocks on the pricing of risk is not a simple matter of a higher price for risk.
